'''Ipili''' is an [[Engan language]] of the East New Guinea Highlands in [[Enga Province]], [[Papua New Guinea]]. The name of the language means 'salt-people' in [[Huli language]].<ref name="BG2011">{{Citation | last1 = Borchard| first1 = Terrance|last2=Gibbs|first2=Philip| year = 2011| chapter = Parallelism and Poetics in Tindi Narratives Sung in the Ipili Language| title = Sung Tales from the Papua New Guinea Highlands| publisher = [[ANU Press|ANU-Press]]| page = 165-195| url = https://library.oapen.org/bitstream/handle/20.500.12657/33603/1/459753.pdf| access-date = 2024-09-13}}</ref> There are 26,000 Ipili speakers.<ref name="BG2011"/>

There are two dialects, Porgera-Paiela and Tipinini. The latter is similar to [[Enga language|Enga]].
Missionary Terrance Borchard guided translation of the New Testament in the Paiela dialect.  Working with the Ipili tribe they developed an alphabet and written language, previously spoken. He began the work in 1969 until his death in Aug. 2014.
Literacy work resulted.

Ipili has five vowels (/a, e, i, o, u/) and thirteen consonants (/p, t, k, mb, nd, nj, ŋg, m, n, s, l, y, w/).<ref name="Franklin">{{Citation | last = Franklin| first = Karl J.| year = 1997| title = Engan pronouns and their old endings| journal = Australian Journal of Linguistics| volume = 17| pages = 185-216| url = https://doi.org/10.1080/07268609708599551| access-date = 2024-09-13}}</ref> It is reported that Ipili may have tonal contrasts.<ref name="Ingemann1980" /><ref name="Franklin" />

In Ipili [[consonant clusters]] do not occur.<ref name="Ingemann1996">{{Citation |last = Ingemann |first = Frances |year=1996|title=Ipili Finite Verb Forms|publisher=Mid-America Linguistics Conference |url=http://hdl.handle.net/1808/23016 |access-date=2024-09-13}}</ref>

===Morphophonology===
[[Progressive assimilation]] and [[regressive assimilation]] can be found in Ipili.<ref name="Ingemann1996"/>

Ipili has [[Vowel harmony|vowel height harmony]], where high and mid vowels are rarely adjacent to each other. By contrast, the low vowel 'a' can be adjacent to any vowel, and thus the word ''mugalo'' 'a variety of bamboo', which contains either high and mid vowel, is found.<ref name="Ingemann1980" />

==Grammar==
===Verbs===
Ipili verbs are inflected for [[Tense–aspect–mood|tense, mood, aspect]], [[Grammatical person|person]] and [[Grammatical number|number]] by [[suffixation]].<ref name="Ingemann1999">{{Citation |last = Ingemann |first = Frances |year=1999|title=Uneventful -ne in Ipili|publisher=Mid-America Linguistics Conference |url=https://hdl.handle.net/1808/23097 |access-date=2024-09-13}}</ref> These suffixes are classified into two groups, tense suffixes and person suffixes. A person suffix is preceded by a tense suffix.<ref name="Ingemann1996"/>

There are three grammatical numbers: singular, [[Dual (grammatical number)|dual]] and plural. Verbs are also inflected by three persons, but second and third person are not distinguished in the dual and plural.<ref name="Ingemann1996"/>

There are a number of tenses and aspects, like a [[present tense]], three [[Past tense|past tenses]]<ref>{{Citation |last = Ingemann |first = Frances |year=1996|title=Ipili Finite Verb Forms|publisher=Mid-America Linguistics Conference |page=209 |url=http://hdl.handle.net/1808/23016 |access-date=2024-09-13}} "Verbs are also inflected for Present tense and for three past tenses, which can be roughly characterized as referring to events that occurred today, yesterday, and before that."</ref> and two [[Future tense|future tenses]].<ref name="Ingemann1996"/>

===Syntax===
The basic word order is [[subject-object-verb]].<ref name="BG2011"/> Ipili [[clause|clauses]] thus place the [[finite verb]] in the final position.<ref name="Ingemann1999"/>

==Literature==
Ipili people have traditional sung tales called ''tindi''. The content may contain something magical.<ref name="BG2011"/>
